Tainan hospital turns to AI for faster emergency patient summaries
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
07:40:23 UTC
16:40:23 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Tainan’s Chi Mei Medical Center has introduced an AI system that can generate a one-page summary of a patient’s medical records in about 30 seconds, helping emergency doctors quickly review key information.
CNA reported Monday that the hospital developed the system with the Ministry of Digital Affairs and Industrial Technology Research Institute. The AI runs on the hospital’s internal systems and summarizes recent treatment, medications, and medical history.
Previously, emergency doctors had to log in to multiple systems and spend five to 10 minutes gathering and organizing patient records. The hospital said the new system reduces that work, allowing doctors to begin clinical assessments sooner.
The system begins collecting relevant records as soon as a patient registers at the emergency department. By the time the doctor sees the patient, the one-page summary is available with a single click.
Doctors can also ask the system specific questions about a patient’s history. It can retrieve information from records created on different dates or by different hospital departments, reducing the need to search through individual records.
The system operates entirely on computers within the hospital and does not require access to the external internet. Keeping it offline helps ensure sensitive medical information remains within the hospital network, strengthening data security and patient privacy, per Liberty Times.
Hospital officials described the system as an “information assistant” rather than a medical decision-making tool. It handles repetitive tasks such as retrieving and summarizing records, while doctors remain responsible for interpreting the information and deciding how to treat patients.
The hospital said the system may also assist with consultations, test planning, explanations of medical conditions, and doctor-patient communication.

'Jealous infatuation': Trial in the murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies begins

Key Points
- Jesse Baird, 26, and Luke Davies, 29, were shot and killed on 19 February 2024 at Baird’s Paddington home.
- The trial is expected to last at least 12 weeks given the number of witnesses to be called.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, "misused his position as a police officer" to stalk Jesse Baird before planning to murder him, a jury has been told as Lamarre-Condon’s double murder trial begins in Sydney.
Jesse Baird, 26, and Luke Davies, 29, were shot and killed on 19 February 2024 at Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney's eastern suburbs.
Their bodies were found eight days later, disposed of in surfboard bags in Bungonia, roughly 200km south-west of Sydney, after the accused handed himself in to police.
Lamarre-Condon stands trial in the NSW Supreme Court on two counts of murder and one count of aggravated break and enter.
He has pleaded not guilty to the charges. He had earlier told the court he would plead guilty to the lesser charge of manslaughter, but this was rejected by the Crown prosecutor.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
Crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC told the 15-person jury that on the day of the murders, Beaumont-Lamarre woke at 4.30am, drove a car he had rented in his mother’s name to Baird’s home, disguised himself as an UberEats delivery driver, entered Baird’s home and allegedly used his NSW Police issued pistol to shoot Baird twice "execution-style".
One of the bullets went through the floor, Hatfield said.
He alleged Lamarre-Condon then shot Davies through the bedroom door.
Hatfield told the court Lamarre-Condon’s "jealous infatuation" with Baird, which formed during their brief relationship, led to “obsessive and compulsive behaviours” that intensified when Baird broke it off in early 2023.
During opening remarks, Hatfield said Lamarre-Condon monitored Baird’s relationships with other men, interfered with Baird’s social media accounts, stalked him, and broke into his home multiple times.
Hatfield said he would present evidence that Lamarre-Condon "misused" his position as a senior constable with NSW Police to obtain CCTV footage of Baird on a date with another man.
Other "obsessive" behaviours detailed to the court included the accused coming to Baird’s home and watching him have sex with other men through the window.
Hatfield alleged Lamarre-Condon also sent messages from a friend’s phone to Baird, where he lied about having a "cancerous tumour growing within his left arm" and was on "medications … which ultimately affects how a person would usually be and react in their day-to-day life".
Lamarre-Condon allegedly broke into Baird’s Paddington home in August 2023 while he was asleep, using a key he had stolen or surreptitiously copied, and stole his phone and wallet.
The court was shown a photo of the bobby pin left in the lock at Baird’s home to give the impression it had been picked.
In subsequent days, Hatfield told the court, Lamarre-Condon "cleaned the scene ... with a range of products and items", "returned the firearm to the [police] safe", and sent text messages from Baird’s phone to give the impression he was still alive and travelling to Perth.
It is alleged Lamarre-Condon drove the bodies of Baird and Davies to Bungonia and initially "tried to sink the bodies in a dam" before burying them in a shallow grave.
Murders were 'pre-meditated and planned'
Members of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies’ family were also in court, some visibly emotional as Hatfield presented details of the alleged murders to the jury.
Hatfield said the accused engaged in significant premeditation and planning before the alleged murders, including hiring a car in his mother’s name and buying a surfboard bag "large enough to fit a person inside".
The court was told Lamarre-Condon stole training bullets from the NSW Police armoury and "experimented with ways he could conceal the sound of gunshots".
During his shift before the murders took place, Hatfield said the accused "pretended to return his service weapon … to a police gun safe" but "retained it despite having no authorised reason to do so".
The trial continues on Tuesday.

The Guards also said they were prepared for a “prolonged war”.

Both sides are maintaining rival blockades in the waterway in an effort to exert pressure.

Afghanistan’s Taliban government denies the charges and says the violence is Pakistan’s internal problem.
The air raids on Monday come days after a Pakistan Taliban faction said it carried out a bombing attack on a mosque at a police facility in Kohat, northwestern Pakistan. The blast and subsequent gun battle killed at least 21 people, mostly police officers, Pakistani officials said.
Pakistan’s Ministry of Information warned Saturday that the country could hit fighters inside Afghanistan in response to attacks in Pakistan. The ministry blamed the Kohat attack on fighters it said were based in Afghanistan.

Erdogan to pursue CAATSA relief, S-400 solution in Trump talks: Fidan
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
07:26:38 UTC
16:26:38 KST

Türkiye has been working to lift US sanctions on its defence industry and resolve the S-400 dispute ahead of an expected meeting between President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and US President Donald Trump, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said.
Speaking to Turkish broadcaster NTV on Saturday, Fidan said Ankara and Washington were exploring “creative ideas” to address the disagreement ahead of the leaders’ expected meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly.
“CAATSA sanctions are an obstacle for us, particularly for our Presidency of Defence Industries. We are working to have them lifted,” Fidan said.
“There are also some creative ideas for resolving the S-400 issue that led to these sanctions. We are trying to put solutions into practice with mutual goodwill. I hope we will take positive steps on this.”
Referring to Erdogan and Trump’s last meeting in Ankara and subsequent contacts, Fidan said the US president had expressed a desire to strengthen bilateral relations and resolve outstanding disagreements.
Fidan did not disclose details of the proposals being considered to resolve the S-400 dispute.
Erdogan has arrived in New York to attend the General Assembly, where Fidan said he would deliver a wide-ranging speech outlining proposals to address global challenges, including a call for joint action on future risks posed by artificial intelligence.
What is CAATSA?
The Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act, or CAATSA, is a 2017 US law that provides for sanctions over significant transactions with Russia’s defence and intelligence sectors.
The measures imposed on Türkiye targeted its Presidency of Defence Industries, known as SSB, and several senior officials, rather than the country’s armed forces or broader economy.
They included a ban on US export licences and authorisations to SSB, restrictions on loans and other financing, and visa restrictions on designated officials.
Removing these measures could ease access to US defence technology and financing and open the way for closer cooperation on military procurement and joint projects.
From S-400 purchase to sanctions
Türkiye’s acquisition of the Russian S-400 air defence system triggered a dispute with Washington, which argued that operating it alongside F-35 fighter jets could compromise the aircraft’s security.
The US removed Türkiye from the F-35 programme in 2019 and imposed CAATSA sanctions in December 2020.
Ankara has maintained that buying the S-400 was a sovereign decision to strengthen its air defences. It rejected US objections and proposed a commission to examine the systems’ compatibility.
Turkish officials have repeatedly criticised the sanctions as unjust and an infringement on national sovereignty.
Trump pledged to lift the sanctions on July 7, speaking before talks with Erdogan in Ankara ahead of the 2026 NATO Summit.
“We’re going to be taking the sanctions off. It’s time to do that… we don't want to sanction friends. It's very simple,” Trump said.

Pakistani fighter jets carried out air strikes on suspected “terrorist” hideouts in eastern Afghanistan on Monday, with Pakistani security officials saying “28 terrorists” were killed, while Afghan authorities reported three civilian deaths and four injuries.
The strikes in Kunar and Paktika provinces threaten to further strain relations between the neighbouring countries after months of cross-border violence and could complicate diplomatic efforts by regional countries to ease tensions.
The casualty claims could not immediately be independently verified. Pakistan's military did not immediately issue a statement on the strikes.
Kabul condemns strikes
Afghan Taliban government spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid condemned the attacks in a post on X and said Afghanistan would respond.
Deputy government spokesman Hamdullah Fitrat said the strikes began around 3 a.m. in Nurgal district of Kunar province and Barmal district of Paktika.
In Nurgal, Fitrat said a house in Pathan village belonging to a resident identified as Noor Ahmad was destroyed, killing Ahmad and two members of his family and wounding four others.
Afghan officials separately said an air strike hit an area housing people displaced by an earthquake.
Fitrat said strikes in Rakhah and Tor Kundi in Barmal destroyed a shop and an unoccupied house but caused no further casualties.
Two Pakistani security officials, speaking anonymously because they were not authorised to comment publicly, said 28 suspected “terrorists” were killed in the operation.
Strikes follow deadly attacks in Pakistan
The air strikes came a day after six Pakistani security personnel, including two army officers, were killed in a shootout with militants in Hangu, a district in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa near the Afghan border.
They also followed Friday's deadly attack on a police facility in Kohat, where a suicide bomber targeted a mosque before armed attackers stormed the compound. The ensuing gun battle lasted about 20 hours and left at least 21 people dead and more than 100 wounded, according to Pakistani officials.
Pakistan's information ministry warned on Saturday that Islamabad could strike militant targets inside Afghanistan in response to attacks on its territory. It accused the Afghan Taliban government of “allowing militant groups” to operate from Afghan soil and called on Kabul to take what it described as credible and sustained action against militant sanctuaries.
No group had claimed responsibility for the Hangu or Kohat attacks by the time of Monday's air strikes.
Dispute centres on Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan
Pakistan has increasingly blamed the Pakistani Taliban, or Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which is banned as a terrorist organisation in Pakistan, for attacks on its police and security forces.
The TTP is separate from Afghanistan's Taliban but is allied with it. Islamabad has repeatedly accused the Taliban government of sheltering TTP leaders and allowing militants to launch attacks from Afghan territory, allegations Kabul rejects.
Relations between the two sides have remained tense since February, when Pakistan and Afghanistan engaged in their worst fighting in years.

Venezuela: Civil Society Organizations call for the renewal of Key UN Fact-Finding Mission
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
07:15:48 UTC
16:15:48 KST

In a joint statement published today, a group of 21 civil society organizations, including Amnesty International, call for the renewal of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela (FFM) and address key questions regarding this special UN mechanism, including what the FFM is and why must it be maintained at least until 2028; how the FFM is complementary to the work of the UN Human Rights Office and international justice mechanisms; and, crucially, how the mission can contribute to the future of Venezuela.
This statement follows an interactive dialogue held at the UN Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva on 18 September 2026, during its ongoing 63rd session, where the FFM presented its most recent findings, and several civil society organizations issued oral statements calling on the Council to renew the FFM’s mandate for another two years.
The FFM concluded that gross human rights violations and international crimes continue being committed in Venezuela under a veil of persisting impunity. They also highlighted the role of groups of armed civilians in the government’s policy of repression and other human rights abuses. These conclusions build on a robust body of work published since 2020. In its reports the FFM has profiled a number of mid- and high-ranking perpetrators, chains of command within intelligence services and security forces, and a state policy against the civilian population who might be considered dissidents that would constitute crimes against humanity, including persecution on political grounds.
The FFM concluded that gross human rights violations and international crimes continue being committed in Venezuela under a veil of persisting impunity. They also highlighted the role of groups of armed civilians in the government’s policy of repression and other human rights abuses.
Background information
The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela is a special mechanism created by the UN in 2019 to exercise scrutiny and investigate gross human rights violations in Venezuela. The importance of its work has been widely recognized and, given its continued relevance, its mandate has been renewed in 2020, 2022, and 2024 for two-year periods.
A resolution to extend its mandate is expected to be considered for voting during the final days of the 63rd session of the UN Human Right Council, between 5-7 October. As in previous resolutions that extended the FFM’s mandate, states in the Americas continue to lead the renewal of the mandate of the FFM. Since 2024, the states that lead this effort are Argentina, Canada, Chile, Ecuador, Guatemala, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

Aleppo governor Azzam al-Gharib urged residents not to leave their homes for the time being, adding that "hospitals, ambulance and emergency teams are on full alert".
Roads leading to the site of the explosions were closed "to ensure the safety of civilians", Aleppo's Internal Security Command was quoted by SANA as saying.
Several such blasts have previously occurred in Syria, which is emerging from more than a decade of civil war following the toppling of longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad in late 2024.

ADAPTABLE WELLNESS ENGINEERING FOR GLOBAL DESIGNERS
Effe merges traditional spa culture with forward-looking design, transitioning saunas from collective facilities into private interiors while reframing wellness technology as contemporary architecture. This approach meets Patricia Urquiola’s sensory-driven vision in Baluar, a collection inspired by medieval bastions. Reinterpreting these defensive, outward-looking fortresses into intimate sanctuaries, the system creates a protective shelter where bathers can unwind, relax, and recharge.
Fostering direct connections between products and users, Baluar is built upon Italian design heritage and advanced spa technology, translating complex conceptual ideas into realized architectural systems. This technical foundation allows Effe to support architects and designers worldwide, adapting each installation to meet spatial layout demands while preserving total functional integrity.
‘Our partnership with Patricia Urquiola is the next stage in the journey we embarked on all those years ago, a journey of coherence and ongoing innovation. Effe has been a visionary pioneer from the very outset, driven by the challenge to transform objects traditionally intended for a specific function into authentic design elements, while still being faithful to tradition. We had the intuition and courage to push the boundaries of convention, reimagining saunas and Turkish baths as actual elements of the furniture and architecture of a space, considering aesthetics an integral part of the wellness experience,’ states Marco Borghetti, Effe CEO.
Baluar collection merges italian craftsmanship and spa engineering to turn conceptual form into physical architecture
ADVANCED THERMAL PRECISION HOUSED BY ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN
Engineered for spatial adaptability, the system combines a sauna and hammam into a modular structure capable of freestanding, embedded, or large-scale spa configurations. Its minimalist linden wood framework in light or dark heat-treated tones uses specialized joinery to withstand high thermal stress and humidity, while narrow vertical grooves accentuate its architectural presence. Overhead, calibrated lighting casts a soft downlight across the fluted timber, amplifying the sense of shelter to deliver an immersive, protective environment.
Beneath its sculptural exterior, the saunas house Effe’s advanced generators that deliver precise thermal stability and pure steam. Combining heat, cold, steam, and quiet rest into a unified system, Baluar creates an intimate, immersive atmosphere where materiality, technology, and well-being converge in a refined architectural language.

Kanyshai Butun
21 September 2026•Update: 21 September 2026
The ruling United Russia party is leading in the country's parliamentary election and on course to secure a constitutional majority, according to preliminary results on Monday.
 
Central Election Commission chief Ella Pamfilova said United Russia secured 57.83%, up from 49.82% in the 2021 parliamentary election, with 95,18% of ballots processed.
 
She said ruling party candidates were also leading in 208 of the 225 single-member constituencies.
 
Pamfilova said United Russia is likely to secure 355 of the 450 seats in the State Duma.
 
The Communist Party got 13.81%, the LDPR 8.98% and New People 7.96%. A Just Russia received 4.96%, just below the 5% threshold required to enter State Duma, the lower house of parliament.
 
The three-day election for Russia's State Duma ended on Sunday, with turnout approaching 59.32%, up from 51.72% in 2021, according to the commission.
 
More than 111 million voters were eligible to cast ballots in voting held at polling stations and through remote electronic voting.
 
Ten parties competed in the federal party-list vote, including the five parliamentary parties — United Russia, the Communist Party, the LDPR, A Just Russia and New People — as well as Rodina, the Communists of Russia, the Greens, the Pensioners’ Party and the Party of Direct Democracy.
 
The Yabloko party was not included on the federal party-list ballot, but its candidates continued to contest single-member constituencies.
 
The election was Russia's first parliamentary vote since 2022 and was held amid the ongoing conflict with Ukraine. Voting also took place in Russian-controlled areas of Ukraine, a move rejected by Kyiv and condemned by some Western governments.

Amedspor wrote a new chapter in Turkish football history on Sept. 20 night, defeating Beşiktaş 3-2 at home to claim the Süper Lig summit heading into the three-week international break.
The hard-fought victory lifted the newly promoted club to 13 points, making it the first team in league history to sit atop the standings after six matches in its debut top-flight season.
“We started the league well and picked up wins. Starting strong is very important if you want to have a good season,” said Amed assistant coach Stef Wils, who attended the post-match press conference after coach Besnik Hasi was sent off.
“I think we’ve done a good job, but as I said, it’s only been six matches,” Wils added.
“There are still a lot of games ahead of us, and we need to keep working this way.”

Beşiktaş responded after the break when star forward Dušan Vlahovic found the back of the net in the 55th minute. However, Amedspor quickly reclaimed their two-goal cushion just four minutes later through Furkan Soyalp.
Orkun Kökçü’s penalty score in stoppage time settled the score.
The result leaves Beşiktaş stranded at 12 points, while Amed enters the international break riding an unprecedented wave of momentum at the head of the Süper Lig table.

“We hadn’t been able to get the points we wanted in recent matches,” he told a post-match press conference.
“We wanted to fix this, win with a good performance, and make it up to our fans. I congratulate my players for winning by a large margin with a great performance today. We dedicate this victory to our fans. We want to continue on our path by improving our game.”
The emphatic win helped clear the air following a rough patch of results, but Kartal acknowledged the intense scrutiny that comes with managing a major club.
“At the slightest negative result, many labels like ‘The coach is at fault, the coach is out of form’ are thrown around,” Kartal said. “We are used to these. We chose our profession knowing this. We have to weather these. We will plug our ears as much as possible to the outside and focus solely on our work.”

The Trump administration is preparing sanctions against the entire ICC - Reuters
Kyiv • UNN
The United States is preparing sanctions against the entire International Criminal Court. The decision could be made as early as this week.
US President Donald Trump's administration has prepared sanctions against the entire International Criminal Court and may announce them in the near future. Reuters reports, citing two sources familiar with the matter, UNN writes.
Details
According to the publication, the Trump administration previously imposed sanctions on a number of ICC judges and prosecutors. US officials also urged the court to withdraw arrest warrants for Israeli leaders and halt its preliminary investigation into US military personnel in Afghanistan. In July, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced a campaign to isolate the court and called on other countries to withdraw from the ICC. At the same time, the US has not yet imposed sanctions directly against the organization as a whole.
"Sources said that sanctions against the court had already been prepared, although the exact timing of the announcement remained unclear," the publication writes.
The Wall Street Journal cited officials who said that the decision could be finalized as early as this week during a meeting of the United Nations General Assembly. Directly targeting the entire organization, as well as entities that cooperate with it, could seriously undermine the court's work, the publication notes.
"Any sanctions imposed by the US Treasury Department against the organization as a whole would prohibit US citizens and companies from providing the court with funds, goods, or services without a license from the US Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). Banks often overcomply with such US sanctions because they depend on access to the US financial system. Among the court's operations that could be affected by sanctions against the organization as a whole are the procurement of IT services and insurance, the hiring of investigators, and the conduct of everyday financial operations, such as paying dozens of US employees, the ICC secretary and president warned," the publication writes.
We remind you
The International Criminal Court condemned the US sanctions against its president and staff, calling them an undermining of the rule of law. The court will continue its work, supporting employees and victims of international crimes.

Beirut port blast case nears indictment, trial after 6 years
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:52:18 UTC
15:52:18 KST

Naim Berjawi and Lina Altawell
21 September 2026•Update: 21 September 2026
- Public prosecutor Mohammed Saab submits prosecution's 270-page opinion to investigative Judge Tarek Bitar
- Beirut Bar Association lawyer Shukri Haddad says indictment expected before end of year, with trials to follow
 
Six years after the deadly Beirut port explosion, the case is approaching a crucial stage with an indictment expected after prosecution recently completed its opinion.
The blast struck Beirut port on Aug. 4, 2020, killing at least 235 people, injuring over 7,000 others and causing widespread destruction across the capital.
Lebanese authorities attributed the explosion to a fire of unknown origin at the port, where large quantities of highly explosive ammonium nitrate had been stored without adequate safety precautions.
 
270-page opinion
Public Prosecutor Judge Mohammed Saab submitted his completed opinion in the Beirut port explosion case to investigative Judge Tarek Bitar last week, according to state news agency NNA.
 
The opinion runs 270 pages and sets out the public prosecution's requests regarding the investigations conducted into the port explosion.
The prosecution completed its assessment five months after receiving the case file from Bitar, who concluded his investigation in late March and referred it to prosecutors for their opinion.
Bitar has charged more than 70 people in the case, including politicians, security and military officials, and public employees.
 
Indictment draws closer
The submission brings the case closer to an indictment by Bitar, Shukri Haddad, rapporteur of the Beirut Bar Association's prosecution office handling the port explosion case, told Anadolu.
"The public prosecution's opinion is the first official document to provide a comprehensive judicial assessment of the facts, and its importance lies in presenting the first judicial account of what happened on Aug. 4," Haddad said.
“The opinion and the findings it contains are not binding on the investigative judge, who may accept or reject them, as the final decision rests with Bitar through his indictment.”
 
Former president mentioned in case
“The prosecution's opinion remains confidential and may only be reviewed by the Court of Cassation lawyer and the investigative judge,” Haddad said. “The final decision rests with Bitar, who determines whether to indict any individual or official regardless of whether that person's name appears in the prosecution's opinion,” he added.
Lebanese news website Asas reported that the public prosecutor held former President Michel Aoun directly criminally responsible for the explosion, citing his knowledge of the ammonium nitrate and his alleged failure to take appropriate action.”
Aoun filed a judicial complaint over what he described as the “fabrication of falsehoods, defamation and disclosure of confidential investigation information.”
According to the complaint, Aoun argued that circulating and promoting false reports distorts the facts, obscures the identity of those actually responsible and creates a media-driven conviction outside the judicial process.
 
Indictment and trial
Trials in the case are expected to begin after the indictment, which is likely to be issued before the end of this year, after which the entire case will be transferred to the Judicial Council, Haddad said.
Lebanon's Supreme Judicial Council is the country's highest special court for cases involving crimes affecting state security, including political assassinations, terrorism and other offenses referred to it by the Cabinet as threats to national security.
According to observers, Saab's opinion details how a 2,750-ton shipment of ammonium nitrate arrived at Beirut port in 2013, was unloaded and transferred to Warehouse 12, where it remained until the 2020 explosion.
The prosecution's opinion summarizes thousands of pages of correspondence, investigation records, confessions and witness testimony and identifies administrative, security, military and judicial responsibilities, without itself constituting an indictment or formal charge.
The investigation has repeatedly stalled amid Lebanon's political divisions, particularly after Hezbollah called for Bitar's removal in 2021, accusing him of politicizing the case. The investigation eventually came to a complete halt in 2023.
Bitar resumed his investigation after Joseph Aoun was elected president in early 2025 and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam formed a new government, while families of the victims have continued to demand accountability for the explosion.

How a famous Freo fan has helped the Lions chase another AFL flag
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:52:09 UTC
15:52:09 KST

Brisbane Lions players have told ABC Sport that a conversation in July with NBA champion Luc Longley has helped the team in its quest for three consecutive AFL premierships.
The Lions play in the grand final this Saturday against the Fremantle Dockers, the team Longley was the number one ticketholder of in 2006 and 2007.
What's next?
ABC Sport will have a live blog of the AFL grand final between Fremantle and Brisbane from the MCG on Saturday.
If the Brisbane Lions win a third straight AFL premiership on Saturday, they will be thanking a former number one ticketholder for the Fremantle Dockers.
Luc Longley, a three-time NBA champion with the Michael Jordan-led Chicago Bulls, knows what it takes to reach the top and stay there.
Longley, a Fremantle native, was also the Dockers' number one ticketholder in 2006 and 2007.
But a meeting the Olympian had with the Lions in July may be the catalyst for Fremantle's downfall this Saturday.
The Lions are in their fourth consecutive AFL decider, and are trying to complete three premiership triumphs in a row and join the list of all-time great dynasties.
Despite finishing third on the ladder and making it to the final day in September, the Lions' 2026 season has not been smooth sailing.
Brisbane lost their opening two matches of the season, conceded a record 86 points in the third quarter of their loss to GWS, were hammered by 76 points against Carlton, and lost the qualifying final by 53 points to an understrength Sydney.
But they have overcome all obstacles to be in another grand final, with several players telling ABC Sport of a meeting with Longley in July which has spurred them on.
"The ability he had to share some of that wisdom and talk to us about what he went through, it was awesome," Lions star Cam Rayner said.
"Just being able to compare and bounce ideas off him and learn things from him about the ability to keep turning up and find that motivation again has held us in good stead."
The Lions had six wins and six losses through 12 games, but were on a five-match winning streak before meeting Longley ahead of their round 18 clash against West Coast in July.
Rayner said Longley's discussions with the team about keeping the desire to win, despite already experiencing success, resonated with the team as they strived for a third consecutive flag.
"The hunger to want to win and to continue to have that success. At the start of the year there were times that wasn't really there in our performances," he said.
"We were dropping in and out of games and struggling to really perform to the level that we could.
"You can't really question the hunger after the game last week. It's back to a level that it needs to be and it's exciting to bring it to this week.
"That's one of the messages Luc Longley brought to us, he said, 'If the game's not going to get you up, you're probably playing it for the wrong reasons'. I feel like that really resonated with a lot of the boys."
Loading Twitter content
Longley was an important part of the Bulls' 1996-1998 championship run, without being the star player.
Michael Jordan was the star of the NBA, while Scottie Pippen, Dennis Rodman and Steve Kerr also enjoyed big-name status.
For experienced Lions' midfielder Jarrod Berry, speaking to a champion who was known for his team-first work ethic was exactly what he believed Brisbane's dynasty has been built on.
"He [Longley] was never the big dog, the star, the whatever. He got more satisfaction out of seeing his teammates succeed," Berry told ABC Sport.
"Our squad is so talented and we've got so many stars and whatever, but it's not necessarily those guys that are making the club so special.
"It's the other guys that are doing all the tough work and hard work and selfless stuff.
"It was really nice to highlight that. It's all about being generous to your teammates and doing it for them."
The Lions are attempting to become the sixth team to win three consecutive V/AFL premierships, and the first since Hawthorn, who did it from 2013-15.
The Lions won three premierships on the bounce in 2001, 2002 and 2003, then lost the 2004 grand final.
The only club to have won three consecutive flags twice is Melbourne, which did it from 1939–1941 and 1955–1957.

Russia Builds Secret Underground Workshops for Shahed Drone Production. Here’s What Satellite Images Reveal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:51:11 UTC
15:51:11 KST

- Category
- World
Russia Builds Secret Underground Workshops for Shahed Drone Production. Here’s What Satellite Images Reveal
Russia is building underground production halls for Geran, a Shahed-derived attack drone, at its Alabuga complex in Tatarstan, according to an assessment published on September 19.
The Dnipro Osint project, drawing on satellite imagery, estimated that roughly 42,000 square meters of subterranean space had already been constructed for the planned production lines. The project treated both the scale of the excavation and its intended use as its own reading of the imagery.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Dnipro Osint concluded that striking the fortified site directly had become counterproductive, describing such attacks as "absolutely impractical from an economic point of view."
Instead, the project identified the drones' production chain as the realistic target set, pointing to:
- powder plants that manufacture the warheads;
- chemical enterprises supplying key components;
- the VNIIR "Progress" plant, whose antennas allow the drones to largely evade Ukrainian electronic warfare.
According to Dnipro Osint, the move underground followed Ukraine's earliest strikes on Alabuga and is advancing quickly. The project noted that the wider Geran ecosystem is becoming steadily harder and more expensive to hit as production shifts underground and supporting infrastructure is dispersed and reinforced.
Satellite imagery from late August recorded at least 10 new workshops and dozens of storage facilities at the site, along with lattice-tower structures erected around the main production areas. The US-based Institute for Science and International Security assessed that those structures could shield the complex from drone and cruise-missile attacks.
The project noted that Moscow was copying Iran, which relocated much of its production and storage underground in response to US and Israeli air superiority.
The Geran is Russia's domestically assembled version of Iran's Shahed-136, a delta-wing loitering munition launched in mass waves against Ukrainian cities.
Alabuga hosts the country's largest drone-production operation. Concealing and hardening that operation complicates Ukraine's long-range campaign against the systems used in strikes on its cities.
Ukraine first struck Alabuga in April 2024, when a drone hit a dormitory at the site's "Alabuga Polytech" college and injured 13 people. Students there, including minors, have been drawn into drone assembly.
The push underground comes after fresh scrutiny of the equipment used in the Alabuga lines. On September 17, 20 pieces of foreign-made industrial equipment were discovered at the complex—lathes, milling and drilling machines, machining centers, industrial robots, and automated assembly systems supplied by firms in China, Germany, Japan, Switzerland, and Iran.

14:50:11 CST
15:50:11 KST

SINGAPORE, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Singapore's labor market remained resilient in the second quarter, but conditions became less favorable for some resident workers as employment growth moderated, retrenchments increased and six-month re-entry rates weakened, the Ministry of Manpower said on Monday.
Total employment increased by 11,400 in the second quarter, marking the 19th consecutive quarter of growth, the ministry said in its labor market report.
Employment of Singapore citizens and permanent residents grew by 2,200, slowing from growth of 5,400 in the previous quarter, while non-resident employment increased by 9,200.
Growth in non-resident employment was driven by work permit holders in the construction and manufacturing sectors.
Retrenchments rose to 4,620 in the second quarter, from 3,830 in the first quarter. The retrenchment rate increased to 2 per 1,000 employees from 1.6 per 1,000 employees.
The increase was driven by business reorganization and restructuring in outward-oriented sectors such as manufacturing, information and communications, and financial services, the ministry said.
The proportion of retrenched residents who re-entered employment within six months fell to 54.9 percent in the second quarter from 60.7 percent in the first quarter. The 12-month re-entry rate remained broadly stable, indicating that "retrenched workers were taking longer to secure new employment," the ministry said.
The ministry's July business expectations surveys pointed to "a positive but cautious labor market outlook." ■

Taiwan mobile data use far exceeds global average
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:46:59 UTC
15:46:59 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Mobile users in Taiwan consume substantially more data than the global average, CTEE reported Monday.
Users in Taiwan consumed an average of 39.7 gigabytes of mobile data per month last year. By comparison, the latest Ericsson Mobility Report put average global consumption at 22 GB per active smartphone and the average across India, Nepal, and Bhutan at 37 GB.
Analysts attributed Taiwan’s high usage to the launch of NT$499 (US$16) unlimited data plans in 2018 and the growing popularity of video platforms. The rapid adoption of generative AI applications has further increased data uploads and downloads.
Usage has continued to climb this year. As of July, Chunghwa Telecom’s 11.3 million mobile subscribers averaged 38.09 GB per month. Taiwan Mobile recorded 46.58 GB and Far EasTone Telecommunications 51.85 GB, putting the three operators’ weighted average at about 44.7 GB.
China recorded average monthly usage of 24 GB last year, while Northeast Asia averaged 23 GB and Southeast Asia and Oceania averaged 21 GB. Average use reached 25 GB in North America and Western Europe and 23 GB in Central and Eastern Europe.
National Communications Commission data showed that average monthly mobile data use stood at 0.43 GB when Taiwan launched 4G services in May 2014. It exceeded 10 GB in May 2016, surpassed 20 GB in 2019, and reached 30 GB in November 2021.
Low-cost unlimited plans have also raised concerns about a small number of extremely heavy users. Industry estimates cited by CTEE put the number of subscribers consuming at least 1 terabyte, or 1,024 GB, per month at more than 1,000. Far EasTone has identified users consuming more than 20 TB in a month.
Far EasTone President Chee Ching (井琪) said such usage was far beyond normal consumer behavior. Compared with the company’s monthly average of 51.85 GB, users consuming between 1 TB and 20 TB use about 20 to 400 times as much data as a typical customer.

Taiwan launches cybersecurity awareness platform
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:46:53 UTC
15:46:53 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan has launched a platform to help the public identify common cybersecurity risks and raise awareness of digital security.
“I hope that cybersecurity becomes a common language across Taiwanese society and part of our daily habits for dealing with the risks of the digital age,” Minister of Digital Affairs Lin Yi-jing (林宜敬) said at a press conference Monday launching the initiative.
Chan Ting-yi (詹婷怡), chair of the Digital Trust Association in Taiwan, said cybersecurity has become an issue of national security and that citizens must understand their role in the security chain.
“Society will have greater resilience against cyber threats when information literacy and digital immunity become part of people’s everyday lives and translate into collective action,” she said.
According to a recent National Security Bureau report, China launched an average of 2.63 million intrusion attempts per day against Taiwan’s critical infrastructure in 2025, targeting sectors ranging from hospitals to energy.
“Taiwan is a honeypot of the free world,” Lin said, referring to a decoy system designed to attract cyberattackers so security experts can study their tactics and develop countermeasures.
However, an analysis by the Taiwan Network Information Center showed that 58.5% of respondents never or rarely verified information they found online.
The Taiwan Cyber Day website features educational content on common types of fraud and emerging tactics. It also includes an interactive game that helps people understand how they respond to online scams and learn how to spot and avoid them.
Chen Hao-wei (陳浩維), Coupang’s chief information security officer, described the platform’s mission as “giving people a digital vaccine.” The website is a joint effort among the government, professional organizations, and private companies.
Tsai Yen-ming (蔡燕明), deputy commissioner of the Criminal Investigation Bureau, said cybersecurity is an important part of fraud prevention, adding that crime rings have increasingly used technology to step up their operations.
Take a step back before answering a call or clicking a link, Tsai urged.
The alliance chose Sept. 21, Taiwan’s National Disaster Prevention Day, as Taiwan Cyber Day to extend the concept of disaster preparedness and build a collective digital defense network, Chan said.

How Can Thin Brick Support High-Performance Buildings?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:45:00 UTC
15:45:00 KST

Masonry is often perceived through its weight, depth, texture, and sense of permanence. Yet these physical qualities also have several implications for the performance of a building envelope. From the thickness of the mortar joint to the weight of the material, every masonry decision is connected to considerations of durability, stability, and long-term performance, while preserving the material character associated with solidity and permanence. At Summer Street Apartments, thin brick offered a way to retain these qualities while accommodating the insulation and envelope requirements of an all-electric, net-zero energy building. Just as importantly, it helped give the project the residential character the architects were looking for.
Building permanent housing with supportive services requires particular attention to how residents experience the building from day to day. It means understanding their current and future needs, providing access to mobility and services, and considering how the spaces themselves can support well-being. Designing layouts that are easy to navigate, maximizing access to natural light, incorporating vegetation, and separating private spaces from shared gathering areas can help a building feel more residential and less institutional. For people transitioning out of homelessness, that distinction can matter from the moment they arrive.
Summer Street Apartments was built on a vacant parcel within the Transit-Oriented Development zone near downtown Providence. The project uses biophilic elements, intuitive wayfinding, and a mix of private and communal spaces alongside high-performance building strategies and net-zero energy goals. Designed by KITE Architects, the project had to combine a high-performance building envelope with a warm and durable exterior within the same wall assembly. The design team selected thin brick from Summitville—a General Shale brand—in a combination of four colors: 26 Savannah, 401 Graphite, B109 Andover Blend, and Aquavue, a blue-glazed finish. A gradient pattern, anchored by a red-brick base, uses shifts in color to add visual depth and recall the masonry character of traditional urban buildings. The upper volumes are set back to respond to the site constraints and create visual interest along the roofline. Several common rooms are distributed along the north façade on the upper levels, providing spaces for gatherings and community interaction.
Thin brick can reduce the thickness and weight associated with masonry cladding while retaining its appearance and surface texture. While a conventional-thickness brick veneer adds weight and depth to a wall assembly, a high-performance envelope also needs space for continuous insulation and carefully detailed air-sealing layers. By reducing the depth of the cladding, thin brick leaves more room within the assembly for these components. At Summer Street Apartments, this helped make brick compatible with the requirements of an all-electric, net-zero energy building without giving up the visual and tactile qualities of masonry.
Performance, however, was only one constraint. The wall system also had to meet a tight budget and construction schedule, requiring close coordination among the manufacturer, installer, mason, contractor, and design team. Energy-efficiency measures, tax credits, and green incentives allowed the project to bring together seven different programs and secure more than $2 million in funding, including programs tied to Zero Net Energy and Energy Star standards. Every material had to contribute to this funding structure, meeting required performance levels without increasing costs or disrupting the construction schedule.
Solar energy—generated both on-site and off-site—is combined with electric systems to keep the building's operating costs low after construction is complete. Together with the use of a low-maintenance façade material, these strategies prepare the building to control costs for decades, demonstrating how a façade decision can influence building performance throughout its life cycle.
 "For residents, this financial and environmental strategy directly translates into more stable and sustainable living conditions. Lower operating costs help maintain affordability, while the building's high-performance design creates a healthier and more comfortable environment." —KITE Architects
At Summer Street Apartments, material selection is closely tied to both construction costs and environmental performance. The project's energy and funding strategies connect decisions made during design and construction with the building's future operating costs. Thin brick plays a specific role in this equation: reducing the depth and weight of the cladding while leaving more room for insulation and high-performance envelope details. In this case, adapting brick to a thinner format allows the building to meet demanding performance requirements while retaining the texture and permanence associated with masonry.

The Bogomolets University &quot;in the crosshairs&quot; of law enforcement: a second vice-rector has now been served with a notice of suspicion
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
09:39:57 EEST
15:39:57 KST

The Bogomolets University "in the crosshairs" of law enforcement: a second vice-rector has now been served with a notice of suspicion
Kyiv • UNN
Vice-Rector Volodymyr Tytykalo has become the second NMU official suspected in the embezzlement case.
Vice-Rector for Economic Affairs of the O.O. Bohomolets National Medical University Volodymyr Tytykalo has become the second university management representative to be served with a notice of suspicion by law enforcement officers as part of criminal proceedings concerning the embezzlement of funds during repair works, UNN writes.
At the end of June, law enforcement officers announced the embezzlement of UAH 15 million during repairs to the facade and roof of one of the buildings of the O.O. Bohomolets National Medical University. At the time, notices of suspicion were served on three people whom investigators describe as accomplices.
According to the case materials, in 2021, during the tenders, the appearance of competition between controlled enterprises was created. A predetermined company won the bidding. A contract was concluded with it, while the cost and scope of the completed works were artificially inflated in the documents. The participants in the scheme transferred the difference in funds to controlled companies and withdrew it in cash.
In this way, according to the investigation, the suspects managed to misappropriate more than UAH 15 million.
It became known that in August, as part of these criminal proceedings, Deputy Rector for Administrative Affairs Yurii Bohdan was served with a notice of suspicion. And now Volodymyr Tytykalo has also come under the scrutiny of law enforcement officers.
The rector signed the contract, while the deputy rectors were served with notices of suspicion
Yurii Bohdan is suspected of aiding and abetting the embezzlement of budget funds on an especially large scale. As for Tytykalo, the details of his suspicion and his role in the scheme are not yet known.
Court documents and our own sources revealed that the case concerns an investigation into the inflation of expenses during repairs to one of the university buildings.
In September 2019, Rector Yurii Kuchyn concluded a contract with LLC "Olster" for the overhaul of part of the roof, including heating for the downspouts and gutters, of the university's morphological building at 34 Peremohy Avenue in the capital. The estimate was approved by the rector's order at UAH 10.9 million, including VAT. Control over the order was assigned to Deputy Rector for Administrative Affairs Bohdan.
However, the work was delayed, and several additional contracts were concluded to extend the repairs. The cost and scope of the work did not change in the supplementary agreements. At the same time, according to the investigators' conclusions, the cost and scope stated in the acceptance certificates for the completed construction works were inflated by almost UAH 2.3 million compared with the actual figures. Under these certificates, the university transferred almost UAH 4 million to the contractor.
It is known that Rector Yurii Kuchyn himself was questioned in this case as a witness.
The NACP issued orders concerning Bohdan and Tytykalo
In June 2025, Rector Kuchyn received orders from the National Agency on Corruption Prevention concerning his deputies Bohdan and Tytykalo—the issue was their ownership of corporate rights in a number of commercial entities. The law stipulates that an official in the management of a legal entity under public law, which a state university is, must, after being appointed to office, transfer corporate rights into management and notify the NACP of this. Apparently, this was not done.
In Bohdan's case, until 2025, his declaration listed as "not transferred" a stake in LLC "Maya Law Bureau" and membership in the Bar Association "All-Ukrainian Collegium of Advocates." In the 2025 declaration, they were no longer listed. As for Tytykalo, his first declaration as deputy rector, for 2018, listed ownership of "BK Audit," as well as stakes in LLCs "Helix Med," "UTsAS," and "Eco Med Group," and in a private university. In the 2024 declaration, which the NACP apparently examined, ownership of "BK Audit" and a stake in "Helix Med" were listed as "not transferred." At present, according to the latest declaration, these rights have already been transferred.
The university rector himself, Yurii Kuchyn, has for years declared salary income from outside employment at LLC "Kapital" (Oberih Clinic), LLC "Harmony of Beauty," and the Dobrobut Medical Center; the first two medical institutions are actively used by the university as clinical bases. Is there a violation or a conflict of interest here? That is a question for the National Agency on Corruption Prevention. There is also the question of the salary received by Kuchyn's wife, Kateryna Bielka, who also works at the university, from Kyivmedpreparat JSC and LLC "Yuria-Pharm," for which the university conducted drug research at its facilities. And also how Kuchyn managed to purchase a Honda VFR 800 motorcycle in 2023, when its market value at the time was over UAH 300,000.
Let us add

Putin’s party set to retain two-thirds Duma majority
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:38:18 UTC
15:38:18 KST

President Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party won a record 355 seats in Russia’s 450-seat Duma lower house of parliament, according to preliminary results from the three-day election released by electoral chief Ella Pamfilova on Sept. 21.
With almost all votes counted from the poll, in which no parties critical of Putin took part, results showed the presidential party will have a supermajority larger than its previous 2016 record of 343 seats.
It was Russia’s first parliamentary election since Moscow launched its Ukraine offensive in 2022.
The Kremlin tightly controls elections and Moscow has banned criticism of its military campaign in Ukraine.
Pamfilova said turnout was more than 59 percent, thanking Russians for voting despite what she called “psychological pressure” on the country.
Russia’s Communist party came second, winning 40 seats.
The nationalist LDPR party took 25 seats and the New People party winning 20 seats.
United Russia has dominated politics since the early 2000s and Putin has been in power since New Year’s Eve 1999.
Pamfilova said that more than 95 percent of votes have been counted and that final results will be announced later this week.
EU top diplomat Kaja Kallas, meanwhile, on Sept. 21 dismissed Russia’s parliamentary elections as a “veneer” of democracy and said she was proposing sanctions on those who helped hold them in occupied Ukraine.
“The so-called Duma elections marked another major setback for Russian democracy. Their outcome was never in doubt,” Kallas wrote on X.
“The Kremlin silenced dissent, barred the only registered party that opposed its war in Ukraine, and shut out international election monitors. The veneer of democracy is all that remains in Russia.”
Kallas said she had “proposed measures against those facilitating these sham elections in occupied Ukrainian territories.”
The EU has already sanctioned some 3,000 officials and entities over the war on Ukraine, including Putin.
The election, held to elect members in all seats of the lower house State Duma, is the first since Moscow launched its large-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
No party opposed to the war was allowed to run, with Russia’s Supreme Court removing the anti-war Yabloko party off the ballot weeks before the vote.
According to results reported by Russian news agencies after just over 71 percent of ballots were counted, United Russia took 57.5 percent of the vote.
The Communist Party and LDPR nationalists trailed behind on 14 and 8.7 percent respectively.

Why China is weighing into the debate on how to respond to shrinking coastlines
Rising sea levels are not an existential threat to China, but their impact on international law could have a knock-on effect in other areas
5-MIN READ5-MIN
 Listen
For low-lying Pacific island states such as Tuvalu and Kiribati, rising sea levels are not just an existential crisis but also one that calls into question the very foundations of statehood.
At the heart of this lies a contentious question: should maritime boundaries shift with changing coastlines, or should they be frozen in place?
The answer carries profound implications not only for the survival of vulnerable islands but also for the rest of the world.
Some analysts have argued that China should position itself as both a legal advocate and technical partner for Pacific nations to offer tangible support – such as surveying expertise, coastal protection technology and advocacy for fixed maritime boundaries.

On the International Day of Peace: Architecture Between Conflict and Coexistence
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:30:00 UTC
15:30:00 KST

Every year on September 21, the United Nations marks the International Day of Peace, an observance that invites global reflection on the conditions necessary to cultivate non-violence, social stability, and human dignity. Under the 2026 theme, "Invest in Peace – For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day," the international body emphasizes that peace is neither static nor self-sustaining. Rather than an abstract condition defined solely by diplomatic agreements, peace operates as an ongoing social process, shaped by economic equity, institutional integrity, and the quality of civic life across communities.
Conflict is also experienced through space. War and political instability can transform homes, public infrastructure, cultural heritage, and landscapes, while displacement can reshape neighborhoods and entire urban regions. Beyond areas directly affected by conflict, questions of segregation, unequal access to resources, exclusion, and the militarization of public space reveal how social and political tensions can become embedded in the built environment.
These relationships between space, conflict, and social life have been explored through a range of architectural and urban projects, from post-conflict reconstruction and emergency housing to the preservation of cultural heritage and the transformation of contested public spaces. Rather than positioning architecture as a solution to complex political conflicts, these examples offer ways to examine how the built environment is affected by conflict and, in turn, how spatial decisions can influence processes of recovery, memory, displacement, and coexistence. Below is a selection of ArchDaily articles that examine these intersections.

(AA Photo)
Egypt has said the Suez Canal remains “safe,” with maritime traffic operating normally along one of the world’s most important shipping routes.
According to a statement from the Suez Canal Authority, Chairman Osama Rabie spoke at a ceremony in Alexandria marking World Maritime Day 2026 organized by the Maritime Transport Sector of the Ministry of Transport.
Rabie said vessel traffic through the canal was proceeding regularly and that revenue reached $567.1 million in August, up 56.7 percent from the same month of 2025.
He stressed that navigation traffic remained stable and services were being provided with high efficiency.
According to navigation reports, 1,358 vessels carrying 68.3 million metric tons of net cargo transited the canal in August, compared with 1,070 vessels carrying 45.2 million metric tons during the same month last year.
Rabie said this represented increases of 27 percent in vessel numbers, 51.1 percent in net cargo and 56.7 percent in revenue.
Referring to global and regional geopolitical changes in recent years, he said international crises had directly affected global supply chains but stressed that the Suez Canal had once again demonstrated its critical and irreplaceable role in securing those supply chains.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty recently said that tensions in the Red Sea had cost Egypt around $11 billion in lost Suez Canal revenues.

====================================================================================================

Does Australia's favourite travel destination hold the secret to a longer life?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:20:08 UTC
15:20:08 KST

In brief
- Ageing populations are increasing worldwide, including in Australia.
- Japan has had a dwindling birth rate and ageing population for decades.
This article contains a reference to suicide.
Long famous for the longevity of its citizens, Japan surpassed a record 100,000 people aged 100 or older this year.
According to the country's health, labour and welfare ministry, Japan's number of centenarians increased for the 56th consecutive year to 107,677 — 88 per cent of whom were women.
Ageing populations are increasing worldwide, including in Australia, where life expectancy, already the third-highest in the world behind Monaco and Japan, is expected to climb over the next 40 years.
According to the Australian government's latest Intergenerational Report, released on Monday, Australia's ageing population is expected to transform the economy.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
As we look to a future with an older population and a longer life expectancy, what lessons can Australia take from Japan?
Henry Brodaty, Scientia professor of ageing and mental health at the University of New South Wales, said there were some obvious differences between Japan and Australia, notably the former's healthier lifestyle: Japanese people largely eat fewer high-fat and ultra-processed foods.
"They eat a lot of fish, which has been associated with a better diet and a lower risk of dementia," Brodaty told SBS News.
He said that social isolation and alcohol intake, both risk factors for dementia, were lower in Japan than in Australia, though Japan had high rates of high blood pressure and vascular disease. Stress levels were also much higher than Australia's.
"In fact, our suicide rate is about 12 to 100,000," Brodaty said. "And theirs is about 16 to 100,000."
Urban supports for longevity
Professor Marco Amati from RMIT University's Centre for Urban Research said Japan has elderly care baked into its urban planning.
"One of the biggest challenges for Australia is to do with aged care facilities, which have many issues; notably, there was a royal commission into that," he told SBS News.
Amati said Japan was good at providing end-of-life care for the elderly, with a clear commitment to providing social housing, public transport, and amenities to a high enough standard as to allow people to "age in place". Amati described this as the "Holy Grail", the "most dignified way to age".
"Everybody would prefer to remain at home, surrounded by your community, age in place, and pass away in a familiar environment," he said.
"If you have a situation where people own their own home, and they have to sell their house to go into aged care, that can be very traumatic."
By contrast, in Japan, housing communities are set up to allow ageing in place, including in rental accommodation or in public housing, and for people with early-onset dementia.
In such places, technological advancements have enabled the monitoring of elderly residents in non-obtrusive ways, ensuring that any end-of-life incidents do not go unnoticed — a common issue for elderly people with few surviving relatives.
Amati said that while similar housing approaches may not be achievable in Australia, they were still useful to know about.
"In Australia it's a whole different mix," he said. "But having that kind of a commitment or even knowing that it exists is useful to know."
Australia's biggest threat to long life
The biggest threat to long life in Australia is dementia, which in 2024 overtook cancer and heart disease to become Australia's biggest killer nationally.
Brodaty quoted recent figures from a US study published in the journal Nature: for people aged 55, the lifetime risk of dementia was 42 per cent.
"It's a scary statistic," Brodaty said.
The earlier people embrace brain health, the higher their chances of living longer. Importantly, Brodaty says, their chances of maintaining good lifetime cognition were higher, too.
"Eating a diet that's rich in vegetables, legumes, extra virgin olive oil, fish, lesser amounts of red meat and sweets, lesser amounts of processed food, watching their blood pressure and getting it checked and treated if it's high," were the best practices, Brodaty said.
Keeping socially connected and having purpose in life were also important. People who live longer "have something that drives them to live and feel valued".
Importantly, Brodaty said there were many simple ways to reduce your chances of getting dementia by almost half.
"We cannot smoke; we can avoid head injury if we can, avoid or treat diabetes. We know that people who have more exposure to green spaces and blue spaces also have a lower rate of dementia," Brodaty said.
"Eating well, remaining socially connected, keeping our brains active, using our brains, being physically active. Exercise is one of the best things we can do for our health in multiple ways."
Living longer, but at what cost?
But the comparison between Australia and Japan can only go so far, Brodaty said.
"We have to consider the demography of the two countries. Australia has 26,270,000 people. Japan has over 100,000,000 people."
Japan's long-lived, ageing population underscores a severe demographic crisis. It's part of the reason the number of centenarians seems "distorted", Brodaty said.
Japan has had a dwindling birth rate and ageing population for decades.
"This is really quite a crisis for Japan economically, because the number of people of working age, proportionately, is decreasing, and the number of people of working age who can look after older people is shrinking."
In Japan, there are roughly two working-age people for every elderly person aged 65 or older.
"Imagine that if we have only one person of working age to help support every older person," Brodaty asked. "How could we possibly arrange our society to deal with that?"
Brodaty said that while this would be an increasing crisis, there was a way to avert it.
"That is to try to help people live their lifespan healthily," he said. "So we talk about healthspan and lifespan, and that gap is what we're trying to narrow."
Readers seeking crisis support can ring Lifeline on 13 11 14 or text 0477 13 11 14, the Suicide Call Back Service on 1300 659 467 and Kids Helpline on 1800 55 1800 (for young people aged up to 25). More information and support with mental health is available at beyondblue.org.au and on 1300 22 4636.
Embrace Multicultural Mental Health supports people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.
For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter.

In a statement, a spokesman for the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said "there will certainly be significant changes in our defence and our counteroffensive" in the event of a new US attack.
"We will introduce new weapons with new capabilities into the battlefield, and the world will be surprised," he said. "Our targets will not necessarily be the same as before either. We have new targets that have not yet been attacked."
The Guards also said they were prepared for a "prolonged war".
On Saturday, the central command of Iran's military said the US was planning new action against Tehran, according to state television, but it did not elaborate.
Fighting between the US and Iran has eased in recent days after a flare-up at the end of last month, though Tehran continues sporadic attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
Both sides are maintaining rival blockades in the waterway in an effort to exert pressure.
The war has spread to Yemen, with the country's Iran-backed Houthis taking more territory from the Saudi-backed government and the group launching attacks on Saudi targets, including the capital Riyadh.
France vows response after Iran closes language centre
France will summon Iran's ambassador and take appropriate measures in response after Iranian authorities sealed a French language centre affiliated with its embassy in Tehran, the Foreign Ministry said on Sunday.
"This new attack against France’s cultural presence in Iran, following the assault on two staff members of the French embassy last July, is unjustifiable and unacceptable," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Pascal Confavreux said in a statement.
Ties between the two countries have been strained for years over Iran's nuclear programme and Tehran detaining several French nationals.
Although the relationship had improved after their release and Paris distanced itself from the US war against Iran, the situation worsened over the summer after two of its diplomats were arrested and subsequently expelled. France reciprocated.
Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency reported earlier on Sunday that authorities had closed the French language centre following a judicial order from the Tehran prosecutor's office.
Iran economy contracts during US war: official statistics
Iran's economy contracted by more than 10 percent during the US-Israeli war, which began with in late February.
The country's gross domestic product (GDP) shrank by 10.1 percent year-on-year from late March to late June, a period known in Iran as the first quarter of the Persian calendar, according to the Statistical Center of Iran on Sunday.
Iran has been at war with the United States since late February, when US-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader and senior military officials at the start of a vast attack.
Aside from this, Iran's economy has long struggled with hyperinflation and devaluation of its currency, caused in large part by economic sanctions.

overlapping concrete walls and columns blur inside and outside in okinawa house
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:15:51 UTC
15:15:51 KST

a large roof unifies a house of overlapping concrete spaces
Overlapping Spaces is a house in Okinawa, Japan, designed by IGArchitects as a composition of reinforced-concrete walls, columns, and a large roof. Rather than dividing the house into conventional rooms, the project creates a continuous spatial field by overlapping structural elements. Walls and columns define different degrees of enclosure, while the large roof unifies the spaces beneath it. The resulting architecture is composed of a series of spaces that are neither completely inside nor outside. Boundaries become ambiguous as views, light, air, and movement pass between the structural elements.
Overlapping spaces define a flexible framework for living
The walls and columns are not treated simply as structural necessities. Their positions establish the rhythm, scale, and sequence of the house, while the roof creates a generous sheltered environment for everyday life. The project reduces the architecture to a small number of strong elements and allows their relationships to generate spatial richness. Instead of prescribing a fixed use for each room, the overlapping spaces provide a flexible framework for different activities and ways of living. Through this project, design studio IGArchitects explores how a strong structural order can coexist with openness and ambiguity, creating architecture that is both defined and adaptable.

Trump welcomes Xi this week amid persistent tensions
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:15:13 UTC
15:15:13 KST

This file photo shows China's President Xi Jinping (R) and U.S. President Donald Trump visit the Temple of Heaven in Beijing, May 14, 2026. (AP File Photo)
When President Donald Trump first ran for office, he called out China as a menace to the U.S. economy, saying it had gutted America’s factories and eroded the middle class.
That tough talk helped Trump get to the White House a decade ago, but since then, he increasingly speaks in glowing terms about Chinese President Xi Jinping, the geopolitical rival Trump will fete on Sept. 24 with a state dinner.
“He’s a great gentleman; we get along great,” Trump said this month. “We have a very good trading relationship and, you know, they’re a competitor and all of that, but we have a very good relationship with President Xi.”
On issue after issue, the Republican president has given Xi a pass.
Trump shrugged off reports that China had provided Iran with satellite imagery, saying, “I think he’s behaved reasonably well.” After accusing Beijing of accessing U.S. voter files back in 2020, Trump indicated he was hesitant to retaliate: “I think China is maybe a little bit different today than it was then.”
Trump’s magnanimity comes as China and the United States are in a contest for global leadership, with some of America’s traditional allies rethinking their strategies. China has expanded its dominance in manufacturing and pushed into new technologies such as artificial intelligence and electric vehicles that create risks for the economies of the U.S., Germany, Italy, France, South Korea and Japan, among others.
Unable to change Chinese behavior, Trump has resorted to hospitality.
He traveled to Beijing in May, and the two leaders could meet again two more times this year at international summits.
Trump has insisted that the U.S. is comfortably ahead of China, but his efforts last year to confront China with a mounting set of tariffs backfired. China holds a relative monopoly on the rare earths used in electronics and deployed that to help force a trade armistice with Trump.
“Trump has dramatically shifted his approach to China because his initial attempt to use super-high tariffs and export restrictions was unsuccessful,” said Michael Kovrig, a senior adviser at the International Crisis Group. “Xi and Trump got into a contest of leverage, and Xi came out on top.”
Meanwhile, Trump has largely undermined the economic and national security alliances that could previously apply pressure on China, said Kovrig.
Trump has mocked French President Emmanuel Macron in speeches. He has run hot and cold on NATO after several of its members did not fully support his choice to start a war with Iran. Trump has launched a potentially brutal trade fight with Canada, a longtime ally he has trolled as becoming the 51st American state.
“He’s executing Xi’s wedge tactics for him, and along the way, helping Xi to tell a story about China as the more stable and responsible power,” Kovrig said. “It’s led to a wave of Western leaders visiting Beijing and seeking to stabilize and improve their relations with Xi so they can focus more on dealing with problems Trump is causing them.”
While Xi met three times on the sidelines of international summits with Democratic President Joe Biden, Trump will have achieved a pair of reciprocal state visits in a sign that the leaders of the world’s two largest economies feel comfortable speaking to each other.
The trade imbalance with China in goods has declined relative to the same period in 2025, according to Census Bureau figures, though the administration has noted that China appears to be routing more goods through other nations such as Vietnam to minimize the tariffs.
Trump’s continued tariffs on China have not curbed its manufacturing sector. China has found new markets and boxed out competition from other industrialized countries. China is exporting more of its goods to the rest of the world with a $1.2 trillion global trade surplus last year as its low-priced EVs undercut the auto sectors in Germany, Japan and South Korea.
Both China and the U.S. are using their trade truce to retrench. China is building up its military and AI capabilities despite limited access to advanced computer chips. The Trump administration has pursued partnerships to develop rare earths.

Grand Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani passes away at age of 98
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-21
06:14:12 UTC
15:14:12 KST

His office announced in the early hours of Monday that “the pure soul of the jurist of the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them) and the exalted authority of the global Shia community, Grand Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani, has joined God.”
The announcement quoted the Quranic verse: “Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, they say, ‘Peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do.’”
The late marja had been admitted to a hospital in the holy city of Qom on Friday evening after a pulmonary complication and remained under intensive care for two days before his passing. Funeral and burial arrangements will be announced later, his office said.
The office offered condolences to the Islamic seminaries, the noble people of Iran, and followers of the marja’iyya across the world. It described his blessed life as one of “deep reflection, continuous scholarly struggle, sincere effort to preserve and elevate authentic jurisprudence, the spread of Islamic teachings, the safeguarding of Shia Islam and goodwill toward the people.”
Grand Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani was born on March 2, 1928, in Qom, three months after his father, the late Ayatollah Sayyid Ahmad Shobeiri Zanjani, settled beside the shrine of Hazrat Fatima Masoumeh (peace be upon her). He was named Musa in honor of that sacred proximity. His father was a prominent jurist, a close associate of the founder of the Qom seminary, Sheikh Abdul-Karim Haeri Yazdi, and a companion of Imam Khomeini in the scholarly circles of the city.
He began seminary studies as a child. He later attended the advanced lessons of leading masters in Qom and Najaf, including Grand Ayatollahs Sayyid Hossein Borujerdi, Sayyid Mohammad Mohaqeq Damad, Sayyid Abolqasem Khoei, Sayyid Mohsen Hakim, Sayyid Abd al-Hadi Shirazi, and Imam Khomeini.
He became one of the foremost authorities in ilm al-rijal, the science of evaluating hadith narrators, and taught advanced fiqh in Qom for more than four decades, according to Press TV.
After the passing of Grand Ayatollah Mohammad Ali Araki in 1994, the Society of Seminary Teachers of Qom named him among the seven jurists qualified for marja’iyya.
